proposal: The Mandate recommends consolidating and elevating the International Trade Administration's Advocacy Center and SelectUSA into a single Office of Trade and Investment Advocacy headed by a Deputy Assistant Secretary. It also recommends that the new office seek congressional authorization to use its foreign direct investment promotion tools to encourage reshoring.

status_summary: A Congressional Research Service report dated 2026-04-15 describes the Advocacy Center and SelectUSA as separate, non-statutory components of Global Markets and reports no consolidation. It notes that the FY2026 request proposed cutting Global Markets funding and staff by more than half, which Congress did not enact, and that an amendment to move Global Markets to the State Department was offered and withdrawn during a House Foreign Affairs markup of H.R. 5248 in the 119th Congress; neither is the recommended consolidation.
title: Consolidate the Advocacy Center and SelectUSA into one trade promotion office
uncertainties: The Commerce rule list on reginfo.gov (labeled Agency Rule List - 2026) lists no rulemaking on the Advocacy Center or SelectUSA; the two ITA entries (RINs 0625-AB27 and 0625-AB30) concern trade remedies and tariff inclusions. The CRS report of 2026-04-15 describes the two units as separate, non-statutory parts of Global Markets; the H.R. 5248 markup date is not stated in its text. The trade.gov About page lists ITA's three business units and does not itemize the two offices. An internal reorganization could exist without a Federal Register notice. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
